Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rk8s (development version)

Controller building blocks

  • Watch gains open(), poll(max_wait) and close(): poll() returns the events that have arrived without blocking for longer than max_wait, and reconnects from the last resourceVersion when the server ends a connection. stream() is now built on them. Events record their own resourceVersion, so a watch stopped part-way through a batch resumes after the last event delivered.
  • Informer gains start(), poll(max_wait) and close(), so one R process can drive several informers from a single loop. poll() relists and reconciles after 410 Gone. run() is now built on them.
  • Watches now run on curl’s multi interface instead of a curl connection. Opening a connection waited for the first byte of the body, and the API server sends none on a resumed watch until there is an event, so an informer on a quiet resource could block for about a minute (until the next bookmark) each time its watch reconnected.
  • New WorkQueue: a queue of object keys with client-go’s semantics. Keys are de-duplicated, never handed out twice at once (a key re-added while in progress is queued again on done()), can be delayed with add_after(), and retried with per-key exponential backoff via add_rate_limited() / forget().

Security

  • pod_exec(), pod_exec_open(), pod_port_forward() and pod_port_forward_open() now verify the API server’s TLS certificate. They previously used the websocket package, which accepts any certificate for any hostname, so the bearer token could be sent to an impersonating server. They now use nanonext (>= 1.10.3, in Suggests instead of websocket and later), verify against the kubeconfig CA (or the system CA bundle) and check the hostname. insecure-skip-tls-verify is still honoured when set.
  • Limitations of the new transport, each reported with a clear error rather than an insecure connection: client-certificate-only users need a token for exec / port-forward, and tls-server-name is not supported for them.
  • Sessions gain pump(timeout) to dispatch incoming frames without blocking for long; PodPortForwardSession gains is_closed(). Frames are dispatched only while wait() or pump() runs (as before, when the later event loop had to be run).

Correctness fixes

  • Typed create/replace calls (AppsV1Api$create_namespaced_deployment() and the other generated write operations) failed with 415 Unsupported Media Type: they sent the spec’s Content-Type: */* literally. Wildcards are now sent as application/json.
  • kube_logs() and CoreV1Api$read_namespaced_pod_log() failed with 406 Not Acceptable (a bare Accept: text/plain is refused by the API server); */* is now offered as a fallback. Untyped generated operations (logs, proxy, …) return text bodies as strings instead of failing to parse them as JSON.
  • pod_exec(stdin_data =) hung until its timeout: the empty stdin frame it sent is not an EOF in the v4.channel.k8s.io protocol. Exec now offers v5.channel.k8s.io (Kubernetes 1.29+) and close_stdin() sends its stream-close message.
  • Watch now delivers events as they arrive. It previously read the stream with a blocking 64 KB readBin(), so small events were held until 64 KB accumulated or the server closed the watch. Requires httr2 >= 1.1.0.
  • Watch$stream(timeout_seconds =), kube_watch(timeout_seconds =) and Informer$run(stop_seconds =) are now real wall-clock limits. Previously the watch reconnected forever after each server timeout, so on a quiet resource these calls never returned. Watch gains end_reason ("stop", "timeout", "gone") and return_on_gone.
  • Informer re-lists after 410 Gone and reconciles its cache, firing on_delete for objects removed while it was disconnected (previously they stayed in the cache forever), on_add for new ones and on_update for changed ones. Lists are paged (page_size, default 500).
  • run_as_leader() can no longer leave two leaders running: on_started_leading now receives a leader handle and must call leader$check() periodically; it signals rk8s_leadership_lost once the lease is lost or renewals stop succeeding, and run_as_leader() then cleans up and calls on_stopped_leading(). Previously nothing noticed a lost lease until the callback returned. The background renewer now uses the full connection settings (client certificates, token files, exec plugins) instead of a bearer token snapshot, which failed on cert-only clusters and expired with exec tokens. Lease updates no longer round-trip managedFields. The lease is released on exit (release_on_exit), and errors from the callback are re-raised after cleanup. Requires callr.
  • Exec credential plugins (EKS, GKE, AKS/kubelogin, …) work again: every call failed in a cache-key helper. They now also receive their input in KUBERNETES_EXEC_INFO (with provideClusterInfo support), keep stderr out of the JSON they parse, pass args and env values containing spaces or quotes intact, honour client certificate/key credentials, include installHint and stderr in errors, parse expiry timestamps with fractional seconds or offsets, and are re-run once when the API server answers 401.
  • A kubeconfig user with tokenFile: sent the file path as its bearer token ($ partial matching read tokenFile as token).

New features

  • KUBECONFIG with several files is merged like kubectl does (first definition wins, relative paths resolve per file).
  • The context’s namespace is read into Configuration$namespace and used as the default by kube() (whose namespace argument now defaults to NULL). In-cluster config reads the service account namespace.
  • Cluster proxy-url and tls-server-name are honoured.
  • OIDC auth-provider users are supported, including id-token refresh; load_kube_config(persist_config = TRUE) writes refreshed tokens back. The removed gcp/azure auth-providers give an actionable error.
  • Ordinary requests are retried (Configuration$max_retries, default 3) on 429 for any method and on 5xx/connection failures for GET/HEAD, with jittered backoff and Retry-After support. New Configuration$timeout.
  • DynamicResource$list() (and so kube_list()) fetches all pages.

rk8s 0.2.1

  • pod_port_forward() (local TCP listener) now works against kind/local clusters. Three correctness fixes folded together:
    • The bridge child process now references the internal bridge_one helper as rk8s:::bridge_one since callr ships the function body into a fresh R process where unexported bindings aren’t injected.
    • The accept loop pumps the websocket event loop via later::run_now while waiting for incoming TCP connections, instead of busy-spinning on blocking=FALSE accept.
    • Local connections are accepted in non-blocking mode so readBin returns immediately with whatever the kernel has buffered. With blocking=TRUE + socketSelect, the local round-trip stretched into seconds for short HTTP exchanges on macOS.
  • Watch no longer hangs on chunks containing exactly one newline-terminated event. R’s strsplit("a\\n", "\\n") returns c("a") (drops the trailing empty piece), which previously made the buffer-based parser keep waiting for “more”. Now we detect the trailing-newline case explicitly. Regression covered by test-watch-buffer.R.
  • New integration tests for exec and port-forward that mint a cluster-admin ServiceAccount token via TokenRequest so the websocket transport (which can’t currently use client-cert auth) is reachable on cert-only kubeconfigs like kind. Lives in tests/integration/helper.R as mint_token_client().

rk8s 0.2.0

High-level verb API

  • New kube() session and idiomatic verbs: kube_get(), kube_list(), kube_apply(), kube_delete(), kube_scale(), kube_logs(), kube_watch(). This is the surface most users want — you never have to type V1Deployment$new(...) to do everyday work.
  • Resource refs accept any of: kind alias ("pod", "po", "pods"), "kind/name" ("deployment/nginx"), explicit "apiVersion:Kind", or c(apiVersion, Kind). Built-in alias table covers the common kubectl shortcodes (po, svc, deploy, sts, ds, rs, cm, sa, pv, pvc, ing, netpol, hpa, pdb, sc, crd, …).
  • as.data.frame() method for rk8s_list returns a tabular view (namespace / name / kind / age / status), so kube_get(k, "pods") is directly viewable.
  • kube_apply() is server-side apply (Content-Type: application/apply-patch+yaml) by default, with force = TRUE conflict resolution and a configurable field_manager.

Pod exec and port-forward (WebSocket)

  • New pod_exec_open() / pod_exec() and PodExecSession. Speaks v4.channel.k8s.io over WebSocket, demuxes stdin/stdout/stderr/error/ resize channels, surfaces the kubelet’s exit code.
  • New pod_port_forward_open() and PodPortForwardSession. Same subprotocol; per-port write() / on_data() API matching the Python client’s design (no local TCP listener required).
  • Both depend on the websocket package (Suggests). Bearer-token auth only — client-cert auth over WebSocket is not yet supported.

Generated layer fixes

  • Critical correctness fix: the generator now resolves $ref parameters against spec$parameters before emitting signatures. Prior versions silently dropped namespace, body, fieldManager, force, and other shared parameters from every namespaced operation — making most generated *_namespaced_* methods unusable. All 944 operations regenerated.
  • PATCH methods now accept an optional content_type argument, defaulting to the spec’s first consumes entry. Pass application/apply-patch+yaml for server-side apply, or application/json-patch+json for RFC 6902 patches.
  • Argument-name collisions in mixed-in operations (notably connect_*_namespaced_pod_proxy_with_path, where path is both a path and a query parameter) are disambiguated with a _query / _header / _body suffix while preserving the wire key.

Other changes

  • Windows: relaxed the URL-assertion in test-client-request.R to decode the query before comparing, fixing a Windows-only failure caused by httr2’s platform-dependent percent-encoding of =.
  • Vignette and README rewritten to lead with the verb API; the typed layer is documented as a drop-down for advanced cases.
  • Integration test suite under tests/integration/ running against a kind cluster, gated on RK8S_E2E=1. New .github/workflows/integration.yaml runs it on push and PR.

rk8s 0.1.0

Initial release.

Runtime

  • Configuration + ApiClient — transport, auth (bearer, basic, client-cert, token-file, exec plugin), TLS, JSON (de)serialization, typed error translation.
  • load_kube_config(), load_incluster_config(), list_kube_config_contexts(), new_client_from_config() — match the semantics of kubernetes.config in the Python client.
  • Watch — streaming line-delimited JSON with 410-Gone resume.
  • Informer + Lister — client-go-style shared cache, initial list plus watch with per-handler add/update/delete events.
  • DynamicClient / DynamicResource — discovery-backed CRUD for CustomResources and any untyped resource.
  • run_as_leader() — leader election against a coordination.k8s.io/v1 Lease, with optional callr-driven background renewer.
  • ApiException + rk8s_api_error condition class.
  • create_from_yaml(), parse_quantity().

Generated API surface (Kubernetes 1.31 OpenAPI)

  • 62 typed API classes (CoreV1Api, AppsV1Api, BatchV1Api, NetworkingV1Api, RbacAuthorizationV1Api, …) covering 944 operations.
  • 635 model classes (V1Pod, V1Deployment, V1ConfigMap, …) with to_list() / from_list() JSON round-tripping.
  • Unstructured scalar types (IntOrString, Quantity, Time, MicroTime, FieldsV1, RawExtension, JSON, Patch, JSONSchemaPropsOr*) emitted as thin value wrappers.
  • JSON-schema meta keys ($ref, $schema) mangled to _ref, _schema on the R side while preserving the literal JSON key on the wire.

Generator

  • tools/gen/generate.R + tools/gen/lib.R — reads a Kubernetes OpenAPI v2 swagger.json and writes R/gen_model_*.R and R/gen_api_*.R. Idempotent; NAMESPACE exports are managed between sentinel lines.
